contacts.name: Katie Boedecker
contacts.title: Owner and Operator (source from 2021, check current)

prospects.fit_notes: Next-generation family owner who also runs a hotel (The Edith) and private mountain rentals, PE programs and youth teams. The family has built its own software in the past, so it is tech-curious and a good candidate for a modern platform.

prospects.name: Hogadon Basin Ski Area
prospects.ownership: City of Casper
prospects.fit_notes: City-run area with ski school and rentals run by separate concessioners, a linked Casper Mountain Ski Patrol organization, and a new-chairlift grant and fundraising effort (Lift Casper). A municipal buyer may want a patrol-only module first.

prospects.name: White Pine Ski Resort
prospects.ownership: Joe Ricketts (purchased 2024)
prospects.fit_notes: New owner (2024) and a new leadership team installed in Nov 2025 at this small two-chair area. A new team with an investing owner is the ideal moment to replace systems.

prospects.name: Antelope Butte Mountain Recreation Area
prospects.ownership: Nonprofit (Antelope Butte Foundation)

contacts.name: Peter Johnson
contacts.title: General Manager (starting October 2026; formerly led Anthony Lakes, OR)

prospects.fit_notes: Community nonprofit (free skiing for ages 17 and under) with a brand-new GM arriving October 2026 as it enters its next development phase. Board resignations over safety concerns were reported, so a patrol and incident-documentation module is a strong pitch.

prospects.name: Ski Santa Fe
prospects.ownership: Independent (owner not named in sources gathered; GM is Ben Abruzzo)
prospects.fit_notes: One of the few remaining independents in New Mexico, after Mountain Capital Partners took over Sipapu, Pajarito and Sandia. Being an independent alternative to the MCP group is a selling angle. Size data not verified in this pass.

prospects.name: Red River Ski & Summer Area
prospects.ownership: Family-owned and operated (Judycki family)

contacts.name: Linton Judycki
contacts.title: General Manager (appointed Oct 2018; source from 2018, check current)

contacts.name: Walt Foley
contacts.title: Deputy GM and Director of Mountain Operations (source from 2018, check current)

contacts.name: Art Mulligan
contacts.title: CFO and Board Director (source from 2018, check current)

prospects.fit_notes: Family-run, in-town ski and summer area with tubing lanes, a zip line and ropes course, and plans to significantly expand summer activities. Its multi-product, year-round operation fits an integrated platform.

prospects.name: Mt. Ashland Ski Area
prospects.ownership: nonprofit (Mt. Ashland Association)

contacts.name: Rachel Canada
contacts.title: General Manager (started Sept 1, 2026; formerly director of mountain operations at Willamette Pass)

prospects.fit_notes: Nonprofit community mountain with a brand-new GM (Sept 2026) and a new patrol director (Jan 2026) alongside a long-running volunteer ski patrol, so leadership is fresh and open to new tools. Store runs on its own domain with no vendor named.

prospects.name: Mt. Shasta Ski Park
prospects.fit_notes: Indy Pass member with 6 lifts, tubing, two terrain parks, twilight skiing and summer biking and disc golf, so it needs many modules in one system. Low-snow closures in 2025-26 put pressure on costs. Ownership not confirmed in sources; verify before outreach.

prospects.name: Diamond Peak Ski Resort
prospects.ownership: community-owned, operated by Incline Village General Improvement District (IVGID)

contacts.name: Kari Brandt
contacts.title: Ski Patrol Director and Safety Coordinator

prospects.fit_notes: Owned by a public district, so purchases go through a public process with board oversight. It has a named patrol director/safety coordinator and a Snowflake Lodge replacement plus master-plan summer ops under discussion. Vertical (1,840 ft) is just over the size guideline.

prospects.name: Tahoe Donner Downhill Ski Resort
prospects.ownership: homeowners association (Tahoe Donner Association)

contacts.name: Annie Rosenfeld
contacts.title: General Manager, Tahoe Donner Association (association-wide, not ski-area specific)

prospects.fit_notes: Small HOA-owned learning hill with a strong ski school and youth programs inside a larger association that runs many amenities, so a single ops platform could cover several of them. No downhill-specific manager was found.

prospects.name: Mt. Rose Ski Tahoe
prospects.ownership: family-owned (Buser family)
prospects.fit_notes: Family-owned independent near Reno and at the top of the size range (8 lifts, 1,800 ft). It's a larger operation with a paid-staff scale that could use the deep patrol module. As of 2024 it had no pass affiliations.

prospects.name: Hoodoo Ski Area
prospects.ownership: locally owned and operated (acquired 1999 by Chuck Shepard of Eugene; current owner not confirmed)
prospects.fit_notes: Locally owned Indy Pass hill with night skiing and the Autobahn tubing park, running lean and focused on 'doing more with less snow.' It's a good mid-size target for an all-in-one platform.

prospects.name: Anthony Lakes Mountain Resort
prospects.ownership: nonprofit (Anthony Lakes Outdoor Recreation Association, ALORA)

current_software.area: online lift tickets, season passes, gift cards

contacts.name: John Wilson
contacts.title: President, ALORA board of directors (as of Nov 2024)

prospects.fit_notes: Nonprofit-run, Thursday-to-Sunday mountain that also runs cat skiing, yurts and camping, a downtown ski shop, and a municipal golf course. That spread fits a multi-module platform. It currently sells tickets through White Peaks Technologies, a small vendor.

prospects.name: White Pass Ski Area
prospects.ownership: local investor partnership (Yakima-based: Andrew Sundquist, David Severn, Dan Plath, Adam Dolsen, Patrick Smith; bought White Pass Co. Inc. Dec 2021)
prospects.fit_notes: Owned by local investors since 2021 and has a large mixed patrol (about 15 paid staff plus about 150 volunteers in 2022), which makes it a strong patrol-module prospect. It was building a new terrain-based learning center and hiring a ski school director in 2024.

prospects.name: Mission Ridge Ski & Board Resort
prospects.ownership: privately owned (Larry Scrivanich, owner and president); owner also bought Blacktail Mountain, MT (2 areas total)
prospects.fit_notes: Independent with a new GM (2025) and planned expansion, and the owner now runs a second area (Blacktail), so one platform across both is a selling point. Its large patrol (27 paid plus 35 volunteers in 2022) fits the patrol module. At 2,250 ft of vertical it's above the size guideline.

prospects.name: Mt. Spokane Ski & Snowboard Park
prospects.ownership: nonprofit (Mt. Spokane 2000) operating in Mount Spokane State Park
prospects.fit_notes: Nonprofit with a large night-skiing program (16 night runs) close to Spokane, so ticketing and staff scheduling see high volume. Above the vertical guideline but within the lift count.

prospects.name: Ski Bluewood
prospects.ownership: local investors
prospects.fit_notes: Locally owned Indy Pass hill adding a high-speed quad and a lift-served bike park (the new lift was delayed as of Aug 2026), so it's growing into summer ops. That's a good moment to replace systems.

prospects.name: Loup Loup Ski Bowl
prospects.ownership: nonprofit (Loup Loup Ski Education Foundation)

contacts.name: Jon Brown
contacts.title: Executive Director (reported departing June 2026 in management restructuring)

prospects.fit_notes: Small volunteer-driven nonprofit that skipped the entire 2025-26 season for lack of snow and is restructuring management to cut overhead. Patrol-only at $149/month or a low-cost bundle may fit, but its finances are fragile.

prospects.name: Leavenworth Ski Hill
prospects.ownership: nonprofit (Leavenworth Winter Sports Club)
prospects.fit_notes: Community club hill (alpine, ski jumping, Nordic, tubing, summer bike programs) that just hired its first executive director, which signals it is professionalizing operations. A small-hill bundle would fit.

prospects.name: Eaglecrest Ski Area
prospects.ownership: City and Borough of Juneau (municipal, board-governed)
prospects.fit_notes: City-owned Indy Pass area with a brand-new GM (Aug 2026), an adaptive program, year-round lodge rentals and summer camps, and a planned gondola for summer 2028. It's a strong candidate for a system refresh.

prospects.name: Arctic Valley Ski Area
prospects.ownership: nonprofit (Anchorage Ski Club), concession with Chugach State Park
prospects.fit_notes: Club-owned nonprofit open on weekends, with the only public tubing park in Southcentral Alaska. Its small staff and volunteer-club culture suit an affordable all-in-one or patrol-only plan.

prospects.name: Hilltop Ski Area
prospects.ownership: nonprofit (Hilltop Youth, Inc.)
prospects.fit_notes: Nonprofit city hill with a busy summer bike park (rentals, camps, race series) and a ski patrol director role posted in 2025-26, so the patrol program is being rebuilt. It is rebranding as 'Hilltop Shred Area' (2026).

prospects.name: Moose Mountain Ski Area
prospects.ownership: privately owned; same ownership since 1993 (owner not named in sources)
prospects.fit_notes: Small independent Indy Pass hill that uses heated buses instead of chairlifts, plus a rope tow. Its public contact is a gmail address, which suggests a very lean operation and likely paper processes. Owner and manager names not found.

prospects.name: Sunrise Park Resort
prospects.ownership: tribal (owned and operated by the White Mountain Apache Tribe)
prospects.fit_notes: Tribally owned, year-round resort (alpine coaster, tubing, zip-line, biking, lodge hotel) investing heavily in snowmaking and renovations. Size not verified and may be above the guideline; confirm lift count.
